instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Diagnostic imaging center network with 12 locations offering MRI, CT, ultrasound, and X-ray services. Processing 80,000 exams per year. Radiologist team of 25 reading remotely across subspecialties. Evaluating AI-assisted detection tools for mammography and lung nodule analysis with radiologist-in-the-loop workflow. The company has mature core business processes but struggles with the tension between running the existing operation efficiently and carving out resources for innovation. We have pockets of digital maturity in specific teams while other areas rely heavily on manual workflows and spreadsheets.
answers.pastInitiatives: We have never run a formal innovation initiative. Problems are solved ad-hoc as they arise, usually by the most directly affected team member. There is no dedicated budget, no structured ideation process, and no track record of experimenting with new technologies or business models beyond basic operational necessity.
answers.strategicGoals: We are the incumbent market leader but face increasing pressure from 2 well-funded new entrants who are undercutting our pricing and offering a more modern customer experience. Our priority is defending our installed base — reducing churn, strengthening switching costs, and matching the digital experience our competitors offer without triggering a destructive price war.
answers.teamSize: Our R&D function consists of 10-12 engineers organized into two squads: one focused on core product innovation and one on exploratory/new business model prototyping. We also have 2 dedicated data engineers building our analytics infrastructure. Innovation projects follow a lean startup methodology with clear go/no-go criteria at 3-month checkpoints.
answers.additionalContext: Our industry is facing a pending regulatory shift that will require mandatory carbon emissions reporting and supply chain due diligence starting next fiscal year. We currently have no systematic data collection for these requirements. Innovation efforts must account for compliance infrastructure investment as a non-negotiable prerequisite to growth initiatives.

input.changes_since_last: Major competitor entered our market. Customer churn rising. Need to accelerate digital transformation.

opportunities.title: Implement a Digital Patient Journey Mapping to Reduce Churn
opportunities.rationale: The primary strategic threat is customer churn due to competitor pricing and modern experience offerings. By mapping the patient journey, Synapse can identify friction points in the existing manual workflows (e.g., scheduling, follow-up) and implement targeted digital fixes that strengthen switching costs without requiring a massive platform overhaul.

first_actions: Form cross-functional teams (clinical, operations, IT) to map 3 core patient journeys (e.g., initial consult, follow-up imaging, billing).
Pilot digital improvements in low-risk areas first, such as appointment reminder/pre-screening portals.
Integrate the identified compliance data points (carbon footprint estimation) into the next phase of patient intake forms.
resources_needed: Data Engineering time for process flow documentation
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in documented 'ease of use' complaints by 15% within 6 months.
milestones: Complete mapping and identify top 3 friction points (Month 2)
Pilot V1 digital solution for the highest-impact journey segment (Month 4)

opportunities.title: Establish Mandatory ESG/Supply Chain Data Infrastructure
opportunities.rationale: The pending regulatory shift requiring carbon emissions and supply chain due diligence is a non-negotiable prerequisite. Addressing this proactively builds robust data governance, which simultaneously strengthens operational resilience and creates an early differentiator against competitors who will struggle to adapt.

first_actions: Conduct a gap analysis on existing systems vs. mandatory reporting requirements (scope 1, 2, & 3).
Select and implement a centralized data repository capable of handling disparate operational and supply chain inputs.
Define standardized metrics for carbon emissions collection at the site level.
execution_plan.success_metric: Automated data capture and reporting dashboard for mandatory compliance metrics.
milestones: Regulatory requirement documentation finalized and costed (Month 1)
Infrastructure POC built and validated with core site data sources (Month 3)
Formalized internal SOPs for quarterly ESG reporting initiated (Month 6)

next_steps.action: Formalize the cross-functional process owner for O-001 (Customer Journey Mapping) to prevent ad-hoc decision making.
Dedicate the initial R&D budget solely to establishing the data infrastructure for O-002, treating compliance readiness as a core product requirement.
Implement mandatory 'Innovation Charter' workshops for all department heads to formalize idea intake, resource allocation criteria, and accountability.

key_weaknesses: Culture resistance to structured process change (Ad-hoc problem solving is the default).
Manual workflows and reliance on spreadsheets create systemic data silos and technical debt.
Lack of systematic, proactive preparation for mandatory regulatory compliance requirements.

improvements: Successfully progressed core operational steps (Step 2 & 3 completed) demonstrating execution capability.
The R&D team has proven capacity by adopting a structured 'lean startup' methodology, moving beyond pure ad-hoc work.
persistent_gaps: Strategic implementation of process improvements remains heavily dependent on the willingness of departmental SMEs to participate formally (Culture Gap).
No dedicated, systematized mechanism for identifying and prioritizing innovation based on systemic market threats or regulatory mandates.
achieved_milestones: Confirmation of internal R&D function capacity and adherence to lean methodology.
Identification of the critical need for centralized data infrastructure due to external compliance pressures.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: Increased market threat (competitors) and regulatory complexity (ESG). While execution capacity improved via structured R&D, the underlying systemic weaknesses in process formalization and compliance readiness persist.
